reasons: The cited grant (p0002) is expressly 'revocable' with no qualifier and runs only to 'Customer', while Section 6(a) bars third-party access absent Kubient's prior written approval — so affiliates/contractors have no path in except vendor discretion. That fails the fallback (affiliates on written notice) and sits in the rule's walk-away zone, so a deviation finding is correctly classified.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it extends the licence to Affiliates (with an inline control definition) and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, confirms such access is not prohibited third-party access under Section 6(a) while keeping Customer responsible for their compliance, and replaces at-will revocability with revocation only on expiration or termination under Section 4.

Successor transferability is handled proportionately — the finding notes Section (h)/p0072 already permits assignment to an affiliate, asset purchaser or merger successor, and the redline merely carves that permitted assignment out of the 'non-transferable/non-assignable' restriction rather than duplicating or re-opening the assignment clause.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.641 changed-character ratio) is explained by the rule genuinely requiring the grant's scope and revocability to be rewritten plus one new sentence to neutralise the Section 6(a) interaction; no unrelated commercial terms were altered. Wording is slightly clunky ('license, revocable only upon…') but substantively sound.
The comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the written-notice fallback without lecturing.
